name: LIHEAP — Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program
organization: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS)
description: The Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) helps low-income households pay for heating and cooling costs, weatherization, and energy-related home repairs. Qualified immigrants — including lawful permanent residents, refugees, asylees, and trafficking victims — are eligible for LIHEAP benefits. The program is administered at the state level, with each state setting its own income thresholds and benefit amounts. LIHEAP serves approximately 6 million households annually and can provide one-time payments directly to utility companies, crisis assistance for households at risk of losing heat or cooling, and weatherization improvements to reduce future energy costs.
eligibility: Low-income households including qualified immigrants (lawful permanent residents, refugees, asylees, trafficking victims); income thresholds vary by state, generally at or below 150% of the federal poverty level or 60% of state median income
amount: Varies by state; typical heating assistance ranges from $200-$1,000 per household per year
applicationProcess: Apply through your state or local LIHEAP agency; applications typically open during heating and cooling seasons. Contact your state energy office or call 211 for local application information.
geographicScope: National (all 50 states, District of Columbia, U.S. territories, and tribal organizations)
documentsRequired: Proof of income, utility bills, proof of residency, identification, Social Security numbers for household members, immigration status documentation for qualified immigrants

name: State-Funded Food Assistance Programs for Immigrants
description: Multiple U.S. states operate their own food assistance programs to serve immigrants who are ineligible for the federal Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP). Following the 2025 changes that removed SNAP eligibility for many humanitarian arrivals, these state-funded programs have become critical lifelines. States including California (CalFresh alternatives and CFAP), New York (SNAP supplement), Illinois, Washington, Connecticut, Maine, Minnesota, and others provide state-funded nutrition assistance regardless of federal immigration restrictions. Benefits and eligibility vary by state but typically cover low-income immigrant families, including those with mixed immigration status.
eligibility: Low-income immigrants ineligible for federal SNAP, including undocumented individuals in some states, asylum seekers, parolees, and mixed-status families; eligibility varies by state
amount: Varies by state; benefits generally comparable to SNAP levels
applicationProcess: Apply through local social services or Department of Social Services offices in participating states; NILC maintains a state-by-state guide at nilc.org
geographicScope: Select U.S. states (California, New York, Illinois, Washington, Connecticut, Maine, Minnesota, and others)
documentsRequired: Proof of income, proof of residency in participating state, household composition, identification; immigration status documentation requirements vary by state

name: USCRI Behavioral Health Support Program
organization: U.S. Committee for Refugees and Immigrants (USCRI)
description: USCRI's Behavioral Health Support Program provides culturally and linguistically tailored, trauma-informed mental health services for resettled refugees in the United States. The program offers individual and group counseling, psychiatric evaluation and referral, crisis intervention through a dedicated national hotline, peer support groups, and community wellness workshops. Services are available in multiple languages through bilingual clinicians and interpreters. The program specifically addresses trauma from forced displacement, war exposure, persecution, and the stresses of resettlement. USCRI also trains mainstream mental health providers on cultural competency for working with refugee populations.
eligibility: Resettled refugees, Afghan Special Immigrant Visa holders, asylees, and other humanitarian arrivals in the United States experiencing mental health challenges
applicationProcess: Contact USCRI directly or through local USCRI field offices; referrals also accepted from resettlement agencies, healthcare providers, and community organizations
geographicScope: National (services through USCRI field offices across multiple states; crisis hotline available nationwide)
documentsRequired: Refugee or asylee status documentation; no specific documents required for crisis hotline access

name: NAMI Immigrant & Refugee Mental Health Resources
description: The National Alliance on Mental Illness (NAMI) provides free mental health support resources specifically for immigrants, refugees, and undocumented individuals in the United States. Resources include the NAMI HelpLine (call or text 1-800-950-6264), peer-led support groups, family education programs, and a searchable directory of local mental health providers who serve immigrant communities. NAMI offers multilingual crisis resources and connects individuals with community mental health centers that provide services regardless of immigration status or ability to pay. The organization also operates a specialized guide for immigrants navigating the U.S. mental health system.
eligibility: Any immigrant, refugee, or undocumented person in the United States seeking mental health support; no immigration status requirements
targetDiagnosis: All mental health conditions; specialized resources for trauma, depression, anxiety
applicationProcess: Call or text the NAMI HelpLine at 1-800-950-6264 for immediate support and referrals; find local NAMI affiliates and support groups at nami.org
geographicScope: National (600+ local affiliates; HelpLine available nationwide)
documentsRequired: None required; services are free and confidential

name: Germany Asylum Seekers Benefits Act (AsylbLG)
description: The German Asylum Seekers Benefits Act (Asylbewerberleistungsgesetz, AsylbLG) provides essential welfare benefits to asylum seekers, refugees with temporary protection, and certain other foreign nationals during their initial period in Germany. Benefits include cash or in-kind allowances for food, housing, heating, clothing, personal hygiene, and household goods. The program also covers necessary medical and dental care, including prenatal and maternity services. After 36 months of residence (reduced from prior periods), beneficiaries transition to standard social welfare benefits equivalent to those received by German citizens. The AsylbLG is administered by local social welfare offices across all 16 German federal states.
eligibility: Asylum seekers, holders of temporary residence permits under humanitarian grounds, tolerated persons (Duldung), and persons obligated to leave Germany who have not yet departed
amount: Monthly cash allowance of approximately €460 for single adults (2025 rates); reduced rates in initial reception centers where in-kind benefits are provided
applicationProcess: Apply at the local social welfare office (Sozialamt) in your municipality or at your assigned reception center upon arrival in Germany; registration in the asylum process automatically triggers eligibility
documentsRequired: Proof of identity (passport or ID), registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung), asylum seeker certificate (Aufenthaltsgestattung) or toleration permit (Duldung)

name: Energy Outreach Colorado — Immigrant Energy Assistance
description: Energy Outreach Colorado provides energy assistance grants to community-based organizations that serve immigrant, refugee, and newcomer populations in Colorado. The program funds outreach workers who help immigrant families navigate energy bill assistance applications including LIHEAP, utility company programs, and other resources. In 2026 the organization awarded $605,000 in grants to organizations across Colorado, with priority given to programs demonstrating the ability to serve communities with high representation of immigrant and refugee populations. Services include multilingual outreach, application assistance, energy literacy workshops, and connections to weatherization programs that reduce long-term energy costs.
eligibility: Low-income immigrant, refugee, and newcomer families in Colorado; services delivered through funded community-based organizations
amount: $605,000 total program funding (2026); individual family assistance varies based on need and utility costs
applicationProcess: Contact Energy Outreach Colorado-funded community organizations in your area for application assistance; multilingual support available for energy bill assistance navigation
documentsRequired: Proof of Colorado residency, income documentation, utility bills; specific requirements vary by assistance program

name: USAHello — Free Public Benefits Guide for Immigrants
description: USAHello provides free, multilingual online guides and resources to help immigrants and refugees in the United States navigate available public benefits, social services, and community resources. The platform offers comprehensive information on food assistance, healthcare, housing, employment, education, and legal services available to immigrants based on their immigration status. Content is available in over 10 languages including Spanish, Arabic, French, Somali, Dari, Pashto, Swahili, Burmese, and Chinese. USAHello also offers free online GED preparation classes, citizenship test preparation, English language courses, and a resource directory connecting immigrants with local service providers across the country.
eligibility: All immigrants, refugees, and asylum seekers in the United States regardless of immigration status
amount: Free online resources and educational programs
applicationProcess: Access all resources freely at usahello.org; no registration required for information guides; free account creation for GED and citizenship prep courses
geographicScope: National (online platform accessible nationwide; local resource directory covers all 50 states)
documentsRequired: None required for accessing information; some services may require basic registration
